title: Events & cancellation
lede: The WHATWG event and cancellation trio — EventTarget, Event/CustomEvent, and AbortController/AbortSignal — kept distinct from Node's EventEmitter, and implemented as Node implements them: in TypeScript, subclassable, reached as globals. Dispatch is single-target as in Node (there is no DOM tree). An AbortSignal cancels a fetch — including via AbortSignal.timeout(ms) — but is not yet wired into setTimeout.

entries.name: EventTarget / addEventListener / dispatchEvent
entries.signature: new EventTarget(); addEventListener(type, listener, opts?); removeEventListener(type, listener); dispatchEvent(event): boolean
entries.description: Node's EventTarget (written in TypeScript, like Node's own JavaScript): addEventListener with once/passive/capture/signal and handleEvent objects, duplicate suppression, removeEventListener, dispatchEvent returning !defaultPrevented. A listener's throw is reported as an uncaught exception on the next tick while dispatch continues. Subclassable: class X extends EventTarget.

params.name: type
params.desc: Event type name to register or fire.

params.name: listener
params.desc: A function (called with this = the target) or an object with handleEvent.

params.name: opts
params.desc: once, passive (preventDefault is ignored), capture (part of the listener's identity), signal (aborting removes the listener).

returns.desc: dispatchEvent returns false when a listener called preventDefault().

entries.name: Event / CustomEvent
entries.signature: new Event(type, init?); new CustomEvent(type, { detail }); e.type; e.defaultPrevented; e.preventDefault()
entries.description: Event and CustomEvent with the full property set: type, bubbles, cancelable, composed, defaultPrevented, timeStamp, isTrusted, target/currentTarget, eventPhase, returnValue, cancelBubble, composedPath(), preventDefault(), stopPropagation(), stopImmediatePropagation(); CustomEvent.detail (null by default). Both subclassable.

params.name: init
params.desc: CustomEvent.detail and cancelable are read; bubbles is accepted but ignored.

entries.name: AbortController / AbortSignal
entries.signature: new AbortController(); controller.signal; controller.abort(reason?); AbortSignal.timeout(ms); signal.aborted; signal.reason; signal.onabort = cb
entries.description: The WHATWG cancellation token. An AbortSignal is an EventTarget that fires an "abort" event, plus an aborted flag and a reason. Listen with signal.addEventListener("abort", cb) or the signal.onabort = cb event-handler property (fired together on controller.abort(); = null clears it). fetch(url, { signal }) cancellation works — pre-flight, mid-flight, and via AbortSignal.timeout(ms) — on both the top-level await path and the fiber path inside an http.listen handler: the transfer is torn down and the fetch rejects with signal.reason itself, Node parity — by default a DOMException named AbortError for a manual abort and TimeoutError for a timeout, and a custom abort(reason) value rethrown as-is. DOMException inherits Error, so both instanceof DOMException and instanceof Error hold; new DOMException(message?, name?) is constructible directly.

params.name: reason
params.desc: Optional abort reason stored on signal.reason — any value, type preserved; defaults to an AbortError DOMException. A never-aborted signal's reason is undefined.

returns.desc: The controller, or a signal from AbortSignal.timeout.

differences: `JSON.stringify` of an error-subclass `abort(reason)` yields `{}` — Node serializes the instance's own enumerable fields; `.message`/`.name`, `String(reason)` and `instanceof` are faithful
